To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the channel capacity and diversity gain are path limited in the sense of the number of paths around the base station, while the fading correlation matrix appears in both the channel capacity and the average pairwise error probability.

the channel capacity and the error detection probability of a macrocell MIMO system are limited by the multipath diversity, and they are affected by the array configuration and the correlation of multipath fading.
the ergodic capacity of a macrocell MIMO system under local-to-mobile and -base scatterers is limited by the number, and not by the distribution, of multipaths around a base station.

the information theoretic aspects of the MIMO system in the macrocell environment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MIMO channel capacity is multipath limited, and the multipath limited channel model can be used to evaluate the MIMO system performance in the macrocell environment.
the channel capacity is multipath limited, and the multiplexing gain as well as the diversity gain is limited by the number.

the channel capacity and the average pairwise error probability are limited by the total number of multipaths, and the array size at the base station does not play a significant role in the information theoretic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MIMO channel capacity and error probability performance are limited by the multipath environment around the base station, which is different from the conventional wisdom that the MIMO capacity and error probability are limited by the antenna array size.

the channel capacity and the average pairwise error probability are limited by the same number of multipaths, which implies that the multipath limitedness is an important concept in MIMO system design.
the MIMO system is not limited by either the array size or the fading correlation matrix, but by the multipath environment.
